newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish KI optimistic on Q2 industrial trends.
newsitem.headline: Swedish KI optimistic on Q2 industrial trends.

text.p: The Swedish economic research institute KI said on Thursday it was optimistic about industrial economic trends in the second quarter.
It also said it expected the consumer price index (CPI) to rise one percent over the next 12 months.
Its expectations were based on a survey of Swedish industry, KI said.
In its previous survey in December 1996, industry expected CPI to rise 1.1 percent over the next 12 months.
The industrial sector saw order intake rising also on the previously sluggish domestic market, the thinktank said.
"Increased demand is estimated to mean significant production increases," KI said. It added that companies were still expected to keep cutting down on staff.
Product prices were expected to remain largely unchanged.
The service sector was also optimistic about the second quarter, seeing demand increasing, the thnktank added.
Both sectors expected prices to remain more or less unchanged with the exception of computer companies, which saw higher prices.
